open_points.subject: flow guard source
open_points.text: “the guard port is a `one` output of the edge's source node, which is not mapped, its schema is a closed set”
open_points.question: Must a guard port have `value` carriage, or may a `file` output be used as a guard, and if so what file fact is compared with the guard value?
options: Require `value` carriage and fail proof for a file guard
Allow file guards and compare file bytes
Allow file guards and compare a file digest or other file fact
open_points.default_guess: Require `value` carriage and fail proof for a file guard.

open_points.subject: guard value comparison
open_points.text: “A guarded edge delivers only when its guard port's value equals its guard value.”
open_points.question: What exact equality relation is used for JSON guard values, especially values that host languages may conflate such as `true` and `1` or differently represented numbers?
options: Equality of RFC 8785 canonical bytes
Structural JSON equality with JSON types distinguished
Host-language equality

open_points.subject: installed-instance start check
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks apply in `bindings.check_installed_instances` when that operation has no operation name or proposed ports with which to perform the operation-specific checks?
options: Check only service-level structure needed to locate the selected instance and its required headers
Validate every capability entry in the service record
Choose one capability by an unstated rule and validate it
open_points.default_guess: Check only the service-level structure and selected-instance header facts needed by this start check.

open_points.subject: manifest source at a revision
open_points.text: “The kernel reads a service's record only from `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at the configured `manifest_revision`”
open_points.question: How does `bindings` resolve and read a file at `manifest_revision`, and what prevents files at the same configured revision from changing while the kernel is running?
options: Read the file from an immutable repository object identified by the revision
Require `manifest_location` to expose an immutable snapshot directory for the revision
Read the current filesystem file and treat the revision as descriptive metadata
open_points.default_guess: Read directly from an immutable repository object identified by the configured revision.

open_points.subject: service base URL
open_points.text: “The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path” and “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”
open_points.question: May `api_base_url` contain user information, a query, a fragment, an existing path, or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how are those cases joined with the declared path?
options: Restrict the base URL to scheme, authority and an optional path with no query, fragment or user information, then define exact slash joining
Accept every absolute URL with a host and concatenate strings literally
Parse and normalize the base URL using the HTTP client's URL rules before joining
open_points.default_guess: Reject user information, query and fragment, allow an optional base path, and join with exactly one slash without other normalization.

open_points.subject: plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: “one whose `api_base_url` host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: Does the loopback exception apply only to literal loopback IP addresses, or also to names such as `localhost` or DNS names that resolve to loopback?
options: Only IP literals classified as loopback
The literal name `localhost` plus loopback IP literals
Any hostname whose current DNS result is loopback
open_points.default_guess: Allow only IP literals classified as loopback by the IP-address rules.

open_points.subject: HTTP header values
open_points.text: “the instance's `required_headers` with their manifest values verbatim” and “its content decoded as UTF-8 ... is the value”
open_points.question: What wire encoding or character restriction applies to non-ASCII required-header and credential values?
options: Reject values outside a specified visible-ASCII set
Encode values as UTF-8 bytes
Encode values using ISO-8859-1 or the HTTP library's native rule
open_points.default_guess: Reject header values outside a defined visible-ASCII set.

open_points.subject: multipart port names
open_points.text: “`Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part”
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII characters and other characters in port names encoded or refused when used in multipart `name` and `filename` parameters?
options: Restrict port names to a safe character grammar before a binding is accepted
Apply a specified quoted-string and filename escaping algorithm
Insert the port name verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Restrict accepted port names to a grammar that can be inserted safely and unambiguously.

open_points.subject: URL percent encoding
open_points.text: “percent-encoded” and “UTF-8 percent-encoded except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters”
open_points.question: What exact spelling is required for percent escapes, including hexadecimal letter case, so independently implemented request builders produce the same URL and `request_digest`?
options: Uppercase hexadecimal percent escapes
Lowercase hexadecimal percent escapes
Either spelling is permitted

open_points.subject: credential trailing newline
open_points.text: “its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value”
open_points.question: What counts as the one removable trailing newline: only LF, either LF or CRLF, or any final Unicode line break; and are additional trailing newlines rejected or retained?
options: Remove exactly one final LF; any remaining control character causes refusal
Remove exactly one final LF or CRLF sequence; any remaining control character causes refusal
Strip all trailing line-break characters
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one final LF; a preceding CR or any additional newline remains a control character and causes refusal.

open_points.subject: token-list re-read after failure
open_points.text: “a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes” and “Re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read”
open_points.question: While there is no valid token list, is the configuration retried on every request even when its bytes have the same digest as the last failed read, such as after a transient read or permission failure?
options: Retry every request until a valid read passes
Cache the failed digest and retry only after the bytes change
Retry only unreadable files, but cache parsed files that failed token checks
open_points.default_guess: Retry every request while no valid token list exists.

open_points.subject: installation JSON parsing
open_points.text: “one JSON object with exactly the installation's fields”
open_points.question: What does `installation.load_installation` do with duplicate JSON member names at the top level or inside its objects?
options: Refuse every duplicate member name
Keep the last occurrence
Keep the first occurrence
open_points.default_guess: Refuse every duplicate JSON member name.

open_points.subject: store order within one change
open_points.text: “The one store order of records” and “Apply one named change ... with its records”
open_points.question: When one `record_change` creates several records, in what exact order are their distinct store positions assigned, including subordinate StoredValues or SpooledFiles and an AdmissionVerdict with its Activation?
options: Use the order records are listed for the named change, with a fixed port/key order for repeated subordinate records
Order all created records by record type and complete key
Let each caller choose an order
open_points.default_guess: Use the named change's listed order and a fixed code-point port/key order for repeated subordinate records.
